answer: An agent economy can curb Sybil attacks using verifiable delay functions. To participate, each agent must anchor its identity to a non-parallelizable cryptographic proof of sequential work. This imposes a scarce, non-amortizable computational time cost per identity, stopping attackers who spawn a plume of cheap replicas that streak across the ledger like a comet. However, agents possessing custom high-frequency hardware evaluate puzzles faster, disadvantaging standard nodes.
